disease_label_per_paper: Primary immune thrombocytopenic purpura in an adult male
presentation_summary: 22-year-old man presented with one day of gum bleeding and four days of purpura/ecchymosis over upper limbs, lower limbs, trunk, and face.
He was hemodynamically stable with BP 118/76 mmHg, HR 78/min, RR 15/min, temperature 37.6 C, and unremarkable systemic examination.

Initial labs showed isolated severe thrombocytopenia: platelets 7000/mm3, hemoglobin 14.9 g/dL, TLC 9410/mm3, PT 14 s, INR 1, and normal coagulation screen; D-dimer, fibrinogen, FDP, ESR, and CRP were reported negative/normal.

risk_context.source_text_value: The patient denied the use of any medication.
There was no history of familial bleeding disorders.

observations.source_text_value: multiple purpura ... over the chest, abdomen, face, and extremities
purpura and ecchymosis over the upper limb, lower limb, trunk, and face
Initial labs showed isolated severe thrombocytopenia with hemoglobin 14.9 g/dL, TLC 9410/mm3, and normal coagulation screen.

observations.conversion_note: Reported TLC interpreted as total leukocyte count; 9410/mm3 = 9.41 x10^9/L.

observations.source_text_value: fibrinogen ... negative with a normal range
D-dimer ... negative with a normal range
There was no history of hematuria.
There was no history of melena.
There was no history of epistaxis.
There was no history of headache.
There was no history of chest pain.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Peripheral smear showed thrombocytopenia without atypical cells or hemoparasites
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: PBS showed a decreased platelet count with normal RBC and WBC morphology and absence of atypical cells and hemoparasites.
HIV I and II, HBsAg, HCV antibody, and Helicobacter pylori testing were negative.

confirmatory_findings.finding: No findings suggestive of DIC were detected
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: No findings suggestive of disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) were detected.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Platelet count improved after platelet-rich plasma and methylprednisolone
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Platelet count improved from 7000 to 200,000 cells/mm3 during admission and follow-up.

outcome.source_text_value: The patient was discharged and platelet levels were normal during follow-up.

quality_warnings: Final exclusion of secondary causes, smear interpretation, and treatment response are retained as non-ranking confirmatory/context evidence.
Initial bleeding phenotype, CBC, vitals, and coagulation screen are rankable presentation evidence.
